Conditions raised by zujose

Source: R/conditions.R
zujose_error.Rd

Every error zujose raises inherits from zujose_error, then error and condition, so a caller can catch all of them, or one kind, with tryCatch(). Match on the class, never on the message.

Details

One rule divides the classes: a mistake in the caller's own code is a zujose_argument_error, and anything wrong with what came off the wire is a token error, from zujose_parse_error on. So a key, header or claims argument of the wrong type is an argument error, while a malformed token is a parse error whatever its source. A token that is not one string, such as NULL from a missing HTTP header, is a token error too: callers handle it like any malformed token. Every argument is checked before the token is read, and an argument error names the function the caller called.

ClassFieldsRaised when
zujose_argument_erroran argument is of the wrong type, out of range, or inconsistent with another, such as format = "compact" with several recipients, a key that is not a jwk, or a header member of the wrong type
zujose_parse_errora token, header or key is not well formed, or is not one string, or is over a limit other than keys
zujose_policy_erroran algorithm is not allowed, a crit header is not understood, or a key does not fit the algorithm
zujose_key_errora key is missing, malformed or too weak, or more keys fit a token than jose_limits(keys = ) allows; a key that does not fit the token is a zujose_policy_error
zujose_signature_errora signature or MAC does not verify
zujose_decrypt_errordecryption fails, for any reason, after the header has passed the policy checks
zujose_claim_errorclaima JWT claim is missing or does not match what the caller expects
zujose_expired_errorclaim, time, nowthe token has expired, or is older than max_age
zujose_not_yet_valid_errorclaim, time, nowthe token is not valid yet, or was issued in the future
zujose_audience_errorclaimthe token is not for this audience
zujose_issuer_errorclaimthe token is not from this issuer
zujose_subject_errorclaimthe token is not about this subject
zujose_missing_claim_errorclaima required claim is absent
zujose_unsupported_erroralgorithm, needsan algorithm needs a newer zucrypt than the one installed

The last six inherit from zujose_claim_error, so a caller can catch every claim failure at once or one cause.

Every decryption failure raises the same class with the same message, so that the error cannot tell an attacker which step failed (RFC 7516 section 11.5). Messages never contain key material, decrypted bytes or token text.

Examples

key <- jwk_generate("oct", alg = "HS256")
jwt <- jwt_encode(list(sub = "user-1"), key, expires_in = -120)

# Catch one kind of failure by its class.
tryCatch(
  jwt_decode(jwt, key, algorithms = "HS256"),
  zujose_expired_error = function(e) {
    paste("expired at", format(e$time, tz = "UTC"))
  }
)
#> [1] "expired at 2026-11-12 20:05:38"
